chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Furat ibn Ahnaf,

that one of the Children of Israel complained to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, about the hardness of the heart and the scarcity of tears. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him: 'Eat the lentils.' So he ate the lentils, his heart softened, and his tears flowed.
From him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him),

said: 'A man complained to the Prophet of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) about the hardness of the heart. So he said to him: 'Stick to the lentils, for it softens the heart and hastens the tears.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of eating lentils according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* highlights the spiritual efficacy of lentils (*adās*) as a means to soften the heart (*qasāwat al-qalb*) and induce humility through tears, a practice rooted in the tradition of the Children of Israel and confirmed by Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him). It underscores the Shia scholarly view that dietary habits can directly influence spiritual states, serving as a practical remedy for emotional and spiritual hardness.
